content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain bread with raisins, toasted, is a whole‑grain loaf that combines several cereals (wheat, rye, oats, barley) with added raisins. After baking, the loaf is toasted, giving it a crunchy crust and a richer, slightly sweet aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Multigrain bread provides more fiber and micronutrients than standard white bread.
Toasting enhances aromatic compounds, making the flavor more nutty and sweet.
Raisins retain some of their antioxidant properties even after heat treatment.
Adding dried fruit to bread dates back to ancient civilizations, where it served as a portable energy source.
Toasted bread stays crisp longer when stored in a dry environment.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The blend of grains supplies a substantial amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat, rye, and oats provide thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants from raisins
items.content: Raisins are rich in polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Soluble fiber in whole grains can help reduce LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: Complex carbohydrates combined with the natural sugars of raisins provide lasting fullness.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Made with wheat, rye, and barley, this bread contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar from raisins
items.content: Raisins add natural sugars, which may be a concern for individuals monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Toasted bread is denser and more calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Cereal allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific grains used in the loaf.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted multigrain raisin bread works well for breakfast with butter or cream cheese, as a base for sandwiches, in soups, or as a crunchy side to salads. Cube it and toss into salads for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, wrap it in foil and refrigerate, though the crust may soften.
